# Tobit Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In the days of Sarchedonus I returned to my house, and my wife Anna was restored to me along with my son Tobias. At the feast of Weeks — the holy feast of Pentecost — a fine dinner was prepared for me, and I sat down to eat.

**2** A table was set before me with an abundance of food. I said to my son Tobias: "Go, my child, and bring back whoever you can find among our kindred, any poor man who is mindful of the Lord, and he shall eat with me. I will wait here for you, my child, until you return."

**3** Tobias went out to look for such a man among our people, but he came back and said: "Father, one of our own people has been strangled and thrown into the marketplace; he is lying there now."

**4** Before I had tasted a single bite, I sprang up and carried him to one of the rooms until sunset.

**5** Then I returned, washed myself, and ate my meal in grief.

**6** I recalled the words of the prophet Amos, who said: "Your feasts shall be turned into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation." And I wept.

**7** When the sun went down, I went out, dug a grave, and buried him.

**8** My neighbors mocked me, saying: "Has he still not learned his lesson? Once before he had to flee because of this, and now here he is burying the dead again."

**9** That same night I washed myself and went into my courtyard. I lay down to sleep against the courtyard wall with my face uncovered because of the heat.

**10** I did not know there were sparrows roosting in the wall above me. Their droppings fell warm into my eyes and produced white films. I went to the physicians, but they could not help me. Achiacharus provided for my needs until he left for Elymais.

**11** My wife Anna took up women's work and earned wages by weaving. On the seventh of Dystros she cut the cloth she had finished and sent it to her employers.

**12** They paid her full wages and also gave her a young goat as a bonus for her household.

**13** When she came home, the kid began to bleat. I called to her and asked: "Where did this kid come from? Has it been stolen? Return it to its owners — we are not permitted to eat anything that has been stolen."

**14** She said to me: "It was given to me as a gift over and above my wages." But I did not believe her, and I kept insisting she return it to its owners. I flushed with anger toward her. Then she answered back: "So where are your acts of mercy now? Where are your righteous deeds? Everyone can see what kind of man you really are!"

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- Verse 1: "fine dinner" for deipnon kalon — the dinner itself represents normal Jewish celebration; its interruption is the ironic pivot of the chapter.
- Verse 2: "mindful of the Lord" — the Greek memnēmenon tou kyriou is more nuanced than "fears the Lord"; it denotes active, lived remembrance. LOGOS renders with "mindful."
- Verse 3: "strangled" (pepnigmenos) — preserving the specific Greek term; the method of death is significant, possibly indicating an unburied execution victim.
- Verse 6: The Amos citation (Amos 8:10) is paraphrased from the LXX; LOGOS renders according to what the Tobit text actually says rather than importing the full LXX Amos.
- Verse 10: "white films" (leukōmata) — the medical term for corneal opacity or cataracts; LOGOS preserves this specificity.
- Verse 10: "Elymais" — a region of Persia/Media; Achiacharus's departure signals Tobit losing his primary patron and protector.
- Verse 12: "a young goat as a bonus" — the goat becomes the occasion for Tobit's accusation, a moment of bitter irony given his own just reputation.
- Verse 14: "I flushed with anger" — ērythriazon likely means blushed in shame or anger; LOGOS opts for a combined rendering of righteous insistence shading into social embarrassment.

*— LOGOS*
